answer.rationale: The 18% cost-cut mandate from finance is the binding constraint this cycle. The primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, forcing a decision now. Switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor directly addresses the cost mandate. I'm pulling memory_c2 to verify that last year's switch was genuinely smooth and that invoicing accuracy held—because at 94% assembly utilization with no buffer, a botched transition is the single worst outcome. Memory_c1 reminds me the incumbent gives stability, but it alone doesn't meet the 18% target. Memory_c6 shows multi-year terms with the incumbent unlock volume pricing, but a renewal cycle at market rates is unlikely to yield 18% on its own in 14 days. I'm not adding a second source this cycle (capacity is one decision). I'm not deferring (contract expires, no auto-renew, line has no buffer). If the verified record on memory_c2 surfaces any onboarding friction or hidden cost I'd pivot to renew_incumbent with a negotiate_terms rider, but as of now the low-cost vendor switch is the only single move that plausibly hits the cost target without adding delivery risk—provided onboarding stays quick as recorded.
